title: Crypto Compliance Manifest Generator for Multi-Region Key Rotation Evidence
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Build a Crypto Compliance Manifest Generator (CCMG) that produces compact, signed provenance bundles documenting KMS/HSM key rotation events, residency assertions, and retention metadata across regions. The CCMG will consume rotation events from the key-orchestrator stream, enrich them with attestations (KMS key metadata, HSM certificate chain fingerprints, KMS policy snapshots), and emit immutable manifests that can be archived to an S3-backed evidence store and surfaced in Console. Manifests must be cryptographically verifiable (signed with a Redwood-signing key), compact (<= 128KB typical), and include human-readable summaries for audits. This ticket covers design, a PoC implementation, end-to-end test harness, basic Console integration, and an initial rollout to staging regions.
acceptance_criteria: CCMG produces manifests for automated and manual rotations with consistent schema and stable signing
Manifests include: rotation timestamp, previous/next key IDs, region, residency tag, KMS policy snapshot id, HSM cert fingerprint, agent that triggered rotation, and retention TTL
Signed manifests can be verified with a documented public key and verification CLI
Manifests are stored in the evidence bucket with lifecycle policy and manifest-level retention metadata
Console shows manifest summary and link to raw bundle for rotations in staging regions
End-to-end test validates manifest generation for both KMS and HSM-backed rotations
design_notes: We will use a two-part manifest: a compact JSON header and an optional compressed attachment for verbose logs/artifacts. This keeps common queries small while preserving full forensic data.
Signing: use an internal signing service (signer.redwood-internal) to avoid embedding private keys in services. The manifest header includes signer_id and signature using ES256.
Event ingestion: subscribe to key-orchestrator Kafka topic; implement idempotency via rotation_event_id to avoid duplicate manifests on retries.
Schema versioning: include schema_v and a documented migration plan for v1->v2 changes. Keep v1 conservative to maximize compatibility with auditors.
Privacy: redact tenant PII from manifests by default; provide opt-in flag for enhanced audit mode that includes requestor metadata.
Trade-offs: producing full verbose artifacts increases cost and storage; choose compressed tar.gz attachments and a TTL-preserving lifecycle to mitigate.
Compatibility: manifests must be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments; signer service will be available in Private via a shim that calls customer-managed HSM (follow-up ticket).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (PoC): generate unsigned manifests for internal rotations in staging-east (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Signing + Storage): wire signer service + S3 archive; run in staging-multi-region (1 week)
Phase 3 (Console surface + verify CLI): add manifest summaries to Console and publish verification tool (2 days)
Phase 4 (Canary): enable for a small set of customer rotations in dedicated-testing (1 week)
Phase 5 (GA): enable across hosted regions with opt-out for customers (depends on legal sign-off)
Rollback: manifests are append-only; if issues arise, disable CCMG ingestion and mark affected manifests as 'quarantine' in metadata
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validation, signer integration, and idempotency
Integration test that simulates KMS rotation, HSM rotation (mock certs), and validates manifest contents and signature verification
Property tests to ensure manifest size stays below configured threshold for typical rotations
Chaos test: simulate duplicate event delivery, partial enrichment failures, and signer outage; verify retry/backoff and quarantine behavior
E2E test that exercises Console linking and verification CLI against archived manifests
